title: Considerations for Granting Online Gambling Operator Licence
what_it_is: Considerations for Granting Online Gambling Operator Licence

sections.label: Exempt operator licence questions
sections.summary: A question asks the Minister for Home Affairs about considerations for granting an exempt operator licence for online gambling and measures to contain harm.

sentences.text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai –  2  To ask	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what are the considerations in the grant of an exempt operator licence for online gambling; and (b) in the grant of such a licence, what specific measures will be taken to contain and control the potential of remote gambling to cause harm, especially to young persons, vulnerable persons and society at large.

sections.label: Remote gambling legislation aims
sections.summary: The legislation aims to tackle law-and-order issues associated with remote gambling and protect young and vulnerable persons from harm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The legislation aims to tackle law-and-order issues associated with remote gambling and to protect young persons and other vulnerable persons from being harmed by remote gambling.

sections.label: Global remote gambling growth
sections.summary: Global remote gambling activities were estimated at around US$40 billion in 2015 and grew 6%-8% annually over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Global remote gambling activities were estimated to be around US$40 billion in 2015 and grew at a rate of 6%-8% annually over the past five years.

sections.label: Arrests in one operation
sections.summary: In one operation, 4,000 individuals were arrested across France, Greece, Italy, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, China and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In that one operation, 4,000 individuals were arrested across France, Greece, Italy, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, China and Singapore.

sections.label: Exempt operator regime strategy
sections.summary: The exempt operator regime provides a regulated outlet to divert activities from illegal operators and complements prohibition, blocking, enforcement and public education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The exempt operator regime aims to provide a regulated and controlled outlet, to divert activities from illegal operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It is an integral part of our strategy to deal with the problem of remote gambling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It complements the general prohibition of remote gambling, blocking of access and payments to illegal sites, strict enforcement and promotion of awareness and personal responsibility through public education, outreach and engagement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On one hand, we say that gambling, especially remote gambling is pervasive and very undesirable, but on the other hand, it is kind of legal if you go to the exempt operators like Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Thirdly, if we are doing well for that, would the Government seriously consider investing even more resources in the enforcement of this total ban, which has happened for the last two years, instead of spending more money trying to manage things downstream?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Fourthly, again, would the Ministry or the Government consider a total ban in view of the fact that Singapore has banned many less significant things, such as chewing gum and pornographic materials and so forth.

sections.label: Survey on remote gambling respondents
sections.summary: Out of over a thousand respondents, three in 10 acknowledged remote gambling at least once in the past year, two-thirds aged 25 to 44.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Out of over a thousand respondents, three in 10 	Page: 19 acknowledged that they had engaged in remote gambling at least once in the past year, and two-thirds of them were between the ages of 25 and 44.

sections.label: Illegal remote gambling enforcement
sections.summary: An estimate put 2015 remote gambling at up to S$461 million while banned, and Police arrested over 120 people from 2015 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: One estimate suggested that remote gambling in Singapore in 2015 could well be as large as S$461 million, at a time when remote gambling was banned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Enforcement wise, since 2015 till 2016, Police have arrested more than 120 people involved in illegal remote gambling – syndicates, runners, punters – and these include the 39 arrested during Operation SOGA VI, which was the prelude to Euro 2016.

sections.label: Syndicates shift to online gambling
sections.summary: Police observed syndicates moving from terrestrial to online gambling, running bet exchanges and using WhatsApp and WeChat to collect bets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Over the years, the Police have observed a very obvious shift – syndicates expanding their realm from terrestrial gambling to online remote sphere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Syndicates run bet exchanges for online horseracing, casino gambling, soccer betting and lotteries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Syndicates also use technology – WhatsApp, WeChat – to collect bets, finding ways to circumvent detection and enforcement.

sections.label: Proxy online gambling accounts
sections.summary: Applications for Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club are not automatic, operators vet for exclusions, and two-factor authentication is required for online account access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In response to the Member's first question, when a person uses another person's online gambling account as a proxy ‒ presumably because he may not qualify due to age or because he or she is on the exclusion list ‒ the application for both Singapore Pools and Singapore Turf Club is not automatic, and approval is not given immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The operators are required to vet for exclusions and other requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There is also two-factor authentication every time the real gambler accesses the online account.

sections.label: Monitoring local gambling trends
sections.summary: The Member asked whether local trends are monitored and exempt operators' system data reviewed, and the response was that all trends and available data will be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In her second question, the Member asked whether we monitor local trends and will be looking at the data that is generated from the exempt operators' systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We certainly will look at all trends and all the data that are available.
